summary: Miramichi Airport serves the city of Miramichi in New Brunswick, Canada, functioning as a regional gateway to the Miramichi River valley. The airport supports general aviation, charter operations, and limited scheduled service, connecting the forestry and tourism-dependent region to larger Canadian hubs. Its location provides convenient access to one of the world's premier Atlantic salmon fishing destinations and the scenic landscapes of northeastern New Brunswick.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate at Miramichi Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves general aviation and charter flights, with occasional scheduled regional service. Check current schedules as service can change seasonally.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Miramichi?
A: Miramichi Airport is located a short drive northeast of the city center, typically within 15–20 minutes by car under normal traffic conditions.

Q: Does the airport have customs and immigration facilities?
A: As a smaller regional airport, it does not maintain permanent CBSA (Canada Border Services Agency) staffing. International flights typically require prior arrangement for clearance services.

Q: Is the airport open year-round?
A: Yes, the airport operates throughout the year, though winter weather can occasionally affect flight schedules in this region of New Brunswick.
transport_tips: Renting a car is the most convenient option for travelers, as the airport is located outside the city center and taxi availability can be limited. Pre-arranging ground transportation through your hotel or a local operator is recommended for non-fly-in visitors. The short drive into Miramichi follows well-maintained provincial routes that are generally accessible in all seasons.
local_tip: If visiting during salmon-fishing season (late spring through fall), consider booking a local outfitter in advance—Miramichi is world-renowned for Atlantic salmon angling, and the airport is a common arrival point for fishing parties heading to remote river lodges.
